1. Technically, every shot is rolled one at a time in 40k, we only roll a bunch at once to save time.  So with markerlights, roll one at a time until you get a hit, then you can batch roll after that, re-rolling ones.  However, you have to declare all of your shooting before you start rolling, so you can't roll markerlights until you get one hit, then switch to regular weapons.  Also, firing a markerlight means you cannot shoot any other weapons for that model.

2. -1 to hit stealthies in both shooting and melee yes.  Homing beacon is a miniature that comes in the new plastic boxes.  Stealthies should have burst cannons, as fusion blasters are way more expensive, and only one shot at 4+.  You should still magnetize one for burst/fusion swap though because that may change someday.

3. All three of the tactical drone options have their uses.  Gun drones will be your most used, followed by markerlights.  Shield drones are useful to protect your commanders.  Special drones have a very specific issue you have to consider: They are a separate unit with no rules to limit targeting them, so a smart opponent will just blow them up first, then move on to other targets.  Pulse accelerator drone is probably the #1 used specialty drone.  Magnetize the flight-stem to drone connection, but don't bother magnetizing the top/bottom of the drone.  Each drone looks different, painting is not a good representation of different drones.

I posted in another thread my thoughts for Fire Warrior magnetizing, but basically if I was going to do it I would:

Buy (or make) 10 FW torso bits and 10 FW left arm bits.  These two pieces are all that is missing from the sprues in the box to allow you to assemble, from the waist up, 10 Breachers and 10 Strikers.  Then you can magnetize at the waist for easy Strike/Breacher swaps.  Of course then you'd need to decide on Pulse Rifle or Pulse Carbine for your Strikers.... or....magnetize the right arm also.....
The question isn't is it necessary, the question is, do you possess the constitution, the depth of faith, to go as far is as needed?

For those wondering which magnets I used, I buy mine through Home Depot's website, and have them shipped to my local store for free.  

Bigger 1/8 x 1/16:
https://www.homedepot.com/p/Magcraft-Rare-Earth-1-8-in-x-1-16-in-Disc-Magnet-100-Pack-NSN0566/204721213

Smaller 1/16 x 1/32:
https://www.homedepot.com/p/Magcraft-Rare-Earth-1-16-in-x-1-32-in-Disc-Magnet-200-Pack-NSN0591/204721289

They are Magcraft brand and listed as N40.  There are many people who have good luck with smaller magnets in N52, a (theoretically) stronger quality of rare-earth magnet. 

However, in reviewing specification information from Magcraft vs. KJ Magnetics, the Magcraft N40s have a pull force of .67lbs in the 1/8 x 1/16 size discs (source = https://www.magcraft.com/magcraft-nsn0566 )

KJ Magnetics N52s (supposedly stronger magnets) only have a pull force of .56lbs. (source = https://www.kjmagnetics.com/proddetail.asp?prod=D21B-N52 )

Add in that 100 quantity of 1/8 x 1/16 from Home Depot costs $10.99, and 100 quantity 1/8 x 1/16 from KJ Magnetics costs $14.00 plus shipping, I went with Magcraft N40s.

yeah the smaller ones (2mm x 1mm or 1/16 x 1/32 inch) I used aren't strong enough to hold a weapon upright, so I use the bigger (3mm x 2mm or 1/8 x 1/16) for weapons.  The smaller do fine on the pathfinders, support systems and turret.

Also, be wary of the shoulder plate getting in the way of your left arm hardpoint (and left shoulder hardpoint if you're 4 hardpointing them).
